newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday February 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday February 6.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi rejects a report that Italy will be offered delayed entry into EMU and said the country was "solemnly committed" to meeting membership terms from the start (all).

* In an interview, Prodi says "I am going to see (German Chancellor) Kohl knowing that Italy has the full support from France and Spain...I will tell him that the government has proposed to bring forward the 1998 budget precisely to dispel every doubt (Corriere della Sera).

* An all-party commission of parliament began five months of work to try to draft constitutional reforms. In its first act, the 70-member commission elected PDS leader Massimo D'Alema as its new chairman with the support from at least part of the opposition (all).

* Giuseppe Guzzetti was named as the new chairman of the foundation controlling Milan-based savings bank Cariplo. Guzzetti said the bank's ideal partner would be an Italian bank with a foreign presence (all).
* The Treasury will reportedly exclude a consortium led by Dutch bank ABN AMRO from the bid for yellow page publisher SEAT (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* European plane consortium Airbus confirmed a report that Italian manufacturer Alenia was interested in investing in its $8 billion project to build a superjumbo. The report said Alenia would own a 10 percent stake in the project (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* The Italian stock exchange shrugged off EMU worries and closed at the day's highs. The lira recoverd after an early slide against the mark (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
